purpose: Compare full, absent, and fading QKV spectral feedback on a learned CUDA retrieval task
development_selection: medium task; AdamW and Tiger-full both choose LR 0.001 from passing development-only candidates. LR 0.003 failed binding gates for both on medium. No test inputs existed during selection.
spectral_fade: Strength is one for completed updates 0 through 800 inclusive, cosine fades during 800 to 1200, then is zero. The strength used before each update is recorded. At zero, only spectral collection and corrections stop; RMS/trust adaptation continues and its state is preserved.
primary_metrics: paired final test CE: full minus no-spectral
paired final test CE: fade minus full
secondary_metrics: sampled validation CE and first sampled 90-percent step
first-half model hashes of full and fade
applied QKV delta RMS by slice
learning rate and feedback strength traces
controls: New paired seeds; identical initialization, inputs, minibatch order and LR schedules. Tiger modes differ only in spectral feedback. No QKV RMS intervention; changed update magnitudes are part of the feedback effect. No tuning of fade start/end using these test results.
scope: Controlled retrieval, not language modeling. BF16 is CUDA autocast with FP32 parameter storage and optimizer buffers. Seven primary seeds and two FP32 supplements are not a general optimizer or hardware-parity claim. AdamW is a learned task control. Keep all failures; production defaults remain unchanged.
timing: Diagnostic only; sequential execution and small model prevent throughput claims
